subject: POC trial planning - workload & traffic profile intake (AcmeHealth)
messages:
From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
To: Priya Singh <priya@acmehealth.com>, Alex Johnson <alex.johnson@acmehealth.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Dylan Brooks <dylan.brooks@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 10 Mar 2027 15:12:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Intro + demo — POC next steps / data & traffic intake

Hi Priya / Alex —

Thanks again for taking the call today. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we can get the POC scheduled: 

Summary of today's call:
- Goal: evaluate Redwood to serve summarization + clinical-search assistant for AcmeHealth's provider portal. Primary success criteria discussed: latency under 300ms p50 for 128-token prompts, p95 under 600ms; semantic match > 88% on our internal eval set; cost target ~$0.006 per 1k tokens.
- Scope: 2-week evaluation, sandbox data (anonymized) + a 48-hour traffic replay window from prod.
- Team: Priya (Acme product), Alex (infra/ops), Ben (Sales/POC owner), Marissa (Solutions), Dylan (SRE support).

Immediate asks for workload intake (can you confirm the values below?):
1) Average RPS during peak day: ?
2) Typical prompt length (input tokens) and expected generation length (output tokens) for the use-case.
3) Concurrency targets (simultaneous users/streams) and acceptable queuing/buffer depth.
4) Burst patterns: once-per-minute spikes, sustained bursts, or event-driven spikes?
5) Any ACL/VPC requirements or IP allowlist windows for the trial.

I've attached a quick template (AcmeHealth_traffic_profile_v1.xlsx) — please fill the traffic profile tab with RPS, token lengths, concurrency and a sample 48-hour timeline.

Proposed timeline:
- By Fri 3/12: Acme to return traffic_profile + success criteria confirmation
- Week of 3/15: Redwood sets up sandbox POC environment and schedules a kickoff run with Marissa/Dylan
- 2-week evaluation: 3/16 — 3/30, with a mid-point check on 3/23

Ownership / next steps:
- Action: Priya to share completed traffic profile + example prompt set (due 3/12)
- Action: Ben to share Redwood POC plan draft (attached) and schedule kickoff once profile is received
- Action: Marissa/Dylan to validate infra requirements after profile is received

Thanks — happy to adjust timeline if you need more time.

Best,
Ben Carter
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
ben.carter@redwood.ai | +1 (415) 555-0123

Hi Ben / Marissa —

Thanks — attaching the filled traffic template and a short prompt set. Quick answers inline: 
- Peak RPS: 28 RPS sustained during clinic hours (08:00-18:00 PT); typical baseline 4–6 RPS overnight.
- Prompt lengths: median input ~110 tokens (range 40–320). Output: median 180 tokens (range 30–600).
- Concurrency: we expect up to 18 concurrent interactive sessions during peak (roughly 1.5x the sustained RPS due to multi-step flows).
- Bursts: event-driven spikes when morning batch jobs run (~30–45 second spikes reaching 80–90 RPS for ~2–3 minutes), plus occasional sustained increases during business hours (up to 40 RPS for ~10–15 minutes).
- ACL: we'll need an allowlist for the Redwood sandbox IPs; Alex will share the firewall team contact.

Attached: AcmeHealth_traffic_profile_v1_filled.xlsx; Acme_prompt_examples.txt

Priya

Thanks for the quick turnaround, Priya — this is super helpful. A few clarifying technical questions so we can size the sandbox correctly: 

1) For the 30–45s event-driven spikes reaching 80–90 RPS, is that single burst per day or multiple bursts (e.g., several jobs across the morning)?
2) Are the prompt/output token distributions roughly the same for the batch replay window, or will batch requests be significantly longer? If batch jobs produce >2k tokens we may need to tune sequence handling/segmentation.
3) Do you have preferred model latency targets per route (e.g., critical search route = 200ms p50)? We want to map the routes to instance sizing.

Proposed next steps from Redwood ops side:
- Dylan: I'll loop you in to provision a sandbox with conservative autoscaling and prefix caching enabled.
- Ben: once Alex shares the firewall contact we'll provide the allowlist IPs and an expected maintenance window for onboarding.

I'll draft a proposed instance profile after a quick pass at the filled sheet — target to share by EOD 3/12.

Cheers,
Marissa
Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.ai

Marissa / Ben —

Firewall contact is netops-team@acmehealth.com. They'll accept an allowlist request with the following details: two /32s for the sandbox and an expected test window of 3/16–3/30. I've included the sample 48-hour timeline in the attached spreadsheet (same file).

Also: regarding batch jobs — we run three morning batches (06:00, 07:30, 08:45) which explains the multiple short spikes. Expect 3–4 spikes in the 30–45s window on typical weekdays. If you can size for 100 RPS headroom during those windows that should be safe.

We'll target sending the anonymized replay dataset by 3/15. Let us know once the allowlist IPs are ready so our netops can approve.

Thanks,
